problem:
What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}]?
$$
worked_solution:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $3$rd columns.
